### framing problem

*  dividing sequence of symbols into messages called _framing_
*  individual messages called _frames_
*  various solutions:
   *  have extra symbols for message start/end/etc.
      *  [probably most common with "fast" physical layers]{.myem-only .fragment .custom}
   *  detect electrically if transmission is happening
   *  [choose sequence of bits/bytes to represent "start message"]{.myem-only .fragment .custom}
      *  needs way of "ecsaping" those bits/bytes if they occur within message data

### spare symbols

*  Gigabit ethernet uses scheme with 625 symbols
   *  5 amplitude levels over 4 wires
*  gives room for spare symbols for message start/end/etc.

### "bit stuffing"

*  scheme in textbook called "bit stuffing"
*  use `01111110` to represent "start/end of message"
*  make sure `01111110` doesn't occur within messages accidentally:
   *  on transmission: replace `11111` in message with `111110`
   *  on receiving messages, replace each `111110` with `11111`

### "bit stuffing" example

*  messages: [`011111100`]{style="color: #a0a; text-decoration:underline"} and [`00000111`]{style="color:#aa0; text-decoration: underline"}
*  <code>01111110[0[111110]{style="font-weight: bold"}100]{style="text-decoration:underline; color:#a0a"}011111110[00000111]{style="text-decoration:underline; color:#aa0"}01111110</code>
